title: The Evening Brief: Markets drift lower as Treasury expands sanctions reach
dek: Saturday's tape shows broad crypto weakness across major assets paired with persistent fund outflows from spot Bitcoin ETFs, as regulatory pressure intensifies with new US Treasury sanctions and growing international crypto taxation.
author: GoCheckMyCrypto
key_fact: The desk's boards reveal a market caught between whale accumulation signals and sustained ETF outflows, while fear sentiment deepens and a Treasury action expands sanctions into a major exchange.
bottom_line: Saturday's session paired broad crypto weakness, Bitcoin down 2.25% over seven days and ETF outflows now consistent for two days, with escalating regulatory action as the US Treasury removed a major exchange from the financial system. Whale flows turned sharply off-exchange this week ($4,049 million over the week ending November 08), reversing prior inflows and suggesting renewed accumulation; however, spot ETF outflows of $1,281.7 million over the week through November 6 offset that signal. Fear sentiment hardened to 28, oversold technicals compressed, and stablecoin supply contracted another 4.66% over thirty days. Upcoming regulatory checkpoints include Japan's unnamed measure checkpoint (October 2 passed; the desk's last update was October 4), Russia's unnamed measure checkpoint on December 1, the US CLARITY Act deadline on January 1, 2027, and the EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets checkpoint on October 25, 2027.
body: Crypto markets drifted lower across Saturday's session as the desk's boards showed sustained pressure on spot ETF demand and a widening regulatory perimeter. Bitcoin down 0.39% over 24 hours, Ether down 0.56% over 24 hours, and Solana down 1.58% over 24 hours, with longer-term momentum weakening: Bitcoin down 2.25% over seven days and down 7.23% over thirty days; Ether down 4.05% over seven days and down 12.66% over thirty days; Solana down 4.88% over seven days and down 17.02% over thirty days. Among the largest coins, PUMP down 7.61% over 24 hours led the losers, while NIGHT up 2.82% over 24 hours, UNI up 2.23% over 24 hours, and ARB up 1.78% over 24 hours showed isolated strength.

The desk's Whale Watch board shows a sharp reversal in whale positioning. Over the week ending November 08, $4,049 million moved off exchanges, a dramatic swing from the prior two weeks, which saw $1,319 million move onto exchanges the week ending October 25. Within the latest 24-hour window, $106,913,178 in bitcoin moved off exchanges from OKX, while $100,036,500 in stablecoins moved onto MEXC, suggesting buyers are staged but conviction remains muted. Against this, the desk's ETF flows board shows spot Bitcoin ETFs saw net outflows of $411.9 million on the day, November 6, and net outflows of $1,281.7 million over the week through November 6, a two-day consistent outflow pattern.

Technical positioning reflects defensive conditions. Across major assets, RSI readings sit in oversold territory: Bitcoin's 14-period RSI stands at 37.8, Ether at 29.4, Solana at 22.4, and Cardano at 26.4. MACD signals remain below their signal lines across the board, and the desk's Fear and Greed Index reads 28, firmly in Fear, marking a tightening of risk appetite. Funding rates on OKX remain positive but moderate: Bitcoin at 0.0071 over 8 hours (7.8% annualized) and Ether at 0.0045 (4.9% annualized), suggesting calm leverage despite the macro pressure. Liquidations tilted heavily toward longs: on Bitcoin over the past 10 hours, $314,314 in longs liquidated versus $3,976 in shorts; on Solana over 5 hours, $171,923 in longs liquidated versus $5,483 in shorts.

Stablecoin supply continues to contract. The desk's board shows total stablecoin value at $292.3 billion, down 4.66% over thirty days, signaling sustained redemptions and a narrowing of cash dry powder on-chain.
